"# Walkthrough - Seu Marquinho Streetwear Landing Page

We have designed, built, and validated a premium, high-end e-commerce landing page for the streetwear brand **Seu Marquinho**. The application is powered by Next.js (App Router), Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide React, and Framer Motion.

---

## 🛠️ Changes Implemented

### 1. Project Initialization & File Migration
- Standardized the Next.js workspace using TypeScript, ESLint, App Router, and the `src/` directory.
- Re-migrated the original brand photos under `public/PRODUTOS E LOGO/` using their actual file extensions (e.g. `.PNG`) as present on disk to avoid hydration and load failures in Next.js.
- Installed `framer-motion` and `lucide-react` for graphics and fluid motion animations.

### 2. Mockup Alignment & Custom Styling (`src/app/globals.css`)
- Introduced the **Montserrat** display font for all headings, paired with **Inter** for base text and labels.
- Set up custom theme variables according to the mockup spec:
  - Gold highlight colors (`#ffe179` and `#ffdb58`) for primary buttons, lines, badges, and headers.
  - Charcoal-black surfaces (`#121414`, `#1a1c1c`, `#0d0f0f`) for components, navbar, and footers.
- Implemented class transitions matching the mockup:
  - `.glass-nav`: Smooth backdrop blurs and white transparent border-b lines.
  - `.product-card-hover`: Image scales up on hover and changes the Buy button border to a solid gold `bg-[#ffdb58] text-black` look.

### 3. Fonts & Metadata Setup (`src/app/layout.tsx`)
- Configured native Google Font optimization with `Montserrat` and `Inter`.
- Added SEO metadata tags, search keywords, and Facebook Open Graph configurations.
- Whitelisted the Google User Content domain in [next.config.ts](file:///c:/Users/jorda/OneDrive/Documents/SITE%20SEU%20MARQUINHO/next.config.ts) to permit high-end lifestyle background images.
